message.content:
Build an in-portal **web terminal** for /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 + Prisma; existing ssh2 dep). Customers click "Open terminal" on the Claude Code hub, pick one of their running servers, and get a real shell (xterm.js) in a slide-in panel — so they can run `claude` and start building right there. SECURITY IS CRITICAL (this SSHes as root into customer VMs). Do NOT run git. You MAY run npm install and npx prisma generate. Do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma.

Architecture (build all of this):
1. **Deps**: `npm install @xterm/xterm @xterm/addon-fit ws` (and `@types/ws` as devDep). ssh2 is already installed.
2. **Short-lived token route** — `app/api/terminal/token/route.ts` (POST {serverId}): requires the signed-in user (reuse lib/auth `requireUser`); verify the user OWNS that server (userId match, status RUNNING) — reuse the ownership pattern from lib/actions-server-ops.ts / app/api/files. Mint a short-lived (60s) signed token (reuse the JWE/JWT helper the console uses — look at how app/api/console or the console route signs its token; mirror it) encoding {userId, serverId, exp}. Return it. This token — NOT the session — authorizes the WS.
3. **WS PTY backend** — a standalone Node service `terminal-server/index.ts` (new dir), run with tsx, listening on 127.0.0.1:PORT (env NXEON_TERMINAL_WS_PORT, default 8901). On connect: read the token from the query string, VERIFY it (same secret/helper), load the Server by id, re-check ownership + RUNNING, resolve host/port via lib/sftp `connectionTarget`, get the root password via `serverRootPassword(server)` (from lib/sftp — decrypts rootPasswordEnc). Open an ssh2 client, request a PTY shell, and pipe bytes bidirectionally between the WS and the shell. Enforce: 15s auth/connect timeout, idle timeout (e.g. 10 min no data → close), a max session duration (e.g. 60 min), handle resize messages (client sends {type:"resize",cols,rows}), and close cleanly on either side ending. Never log the password. In SANDBOX mode (lib/sandbox SANDBOX), instead of real SSH, pipe a friendly simulated shell (a message that this is a sandbox + echo input) so staging works without real VMs.
4. **systemd unit** — write the unit file text to `deploy/nxeon-terminal.service` (WorkingDirectory /opt/nxeon, ExecStart `/usr/bin/npx tsx terminal-server/index.ts`, EnvironmentFile /opt/nxeon/.env, User=nxeon, Restart=always) so the parent can install it. Also write an nginx location snippet to `deploy/nxeon-terminal.nginx.txt` showing the `location /terminal-ws { proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8901; ... WebSocket upgrade headers }` to add to the vhost.
5. **Client component** — `components/customer/WebTerminal.tsx` ("use client"): a slide-in panel (right side, ~half screen, responsive full-width on mobile) with a server `<select>` picker (fed the user's running servers as props), a Connect button, and an xterm.js terminal. On connect: POST /api/terminal/token, then open `new WebSocket("wss://"+location.host+"/terminal-ws?token=...")`, wire xterm ↔ ws, use FitAddon + a resize observer sending resize messages. Import xterm CSS. Show connection status + a Close button. Handle disconnect/errors gracefully.
6. **Wire into the hub** — in `components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx`, add a prominent "Open terminal & start building" button in the hero (it already receives `servers`). Clicking it opens the WebTerminal panel (mount it, pass the servers). If the user has no running server, disable it with a hint to deploy one. Keep the existing content intact.

Verify: `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` clean for your files, and `npm run build` exits 0 (the standalone terminal-server/ is run by tsx, not built by Next — make sure Next doesn't try to compile it; put it outside app/ and don't import it from app code). Report: files created, the exact token verification + ownership checks, the timeouts enforced, and the systemd/nginx snippets' locations.

content.content:
## 8. Subsystems — how each works

**Provisioning (deploying a server).** `orderServer` runs on the server when the deploy wizard is
submitted. It validates the chosen plan, image, term, and add-ons against capacity and the image's
requirements (e.g. minimum RAM), then **atomically debits the wallet** for the first term (plus the
dedicated-IP surcharge if selected) and, in the same transaction, creates the `Server` row and a
`PROVISION` job. The worker picks up the job and: resolves the server's node via `pveFor`, **clones**
the base template onto the correct storage tier, writes a **per-server cloud-init snippet** (SSH
keys, the generated root password, the image's `setupScript`, and any add-on installs), resizes the
disk to the plan size, configures networking (NAT on `vmbr1` **or** a dedicated IP on `vmbr0` via an
OVH Virtual MAC), starts the VM, and notifies the owner. If a step fails the job is **retried up to
3 times**; a **reaper** on worker startup re-queues any job left "running" by a crash so no server
gets permanently stuck.

**Networking.** The default is **shared NAT**: the VM gets a private `10.20.0.x` address, and its SSH
port is DNAT-forwarded to a public port in the `20000–29999` range through the `NXEON_FWD` iptables
chain, which `worker/network.ts` rebuilds from the database. Customers can open additional TCP/UDP
forwards. The alternative is a **dedicated public IPv4** (OVH failover IP + Virtual MAC on `vmbr0`,
no NAT) for customers who need their own address. Free IPv6 for all servers is planned.

**Billing.** Money is tracked as a **prepaid wallet** in integer cents; every charge is an atomic
conditional debit (`wallet.ts`) so races can't overdraw it. Customers add funds through **Stripe
Checkout**; the wallet is credited on the success-redirect confirm route, idempotently keyed by the
Stripe session so a double-load can't double-credit. **Commitment discounts** (`billing-terms.ts`):
VPS is **−10%** annual, **−15%** for 2 years, **−20%** for 3 years; domains get **−5% / −10%** for
multi-year. A **renewal sweep** runs every ~10 minutes: it auto-renews due servers from the wallet,
sends a warning before a server is at risk, grants a **3-day grace** period on failure, then
**suspends**, and finally **terminates** after the termination window — reclaiming the disk and any
dedicated IP. It also auto-renews domains. Every charge produces an invoice (printable / PDF).

**Domains.** Backed by name.com v4. `checkDomains` returns both the **retail** price (Nxeon's
wholesale **cost** plus `DOMAIN_MARKUP_PCT`, default **25%**) and the cost. The customer is charged
retail; name.com is paid cost; the difference is Nxeon's margin, and both numbers are stored on the
`Domain` row so margin is auditable. The flow includes a **register wizard**
(domain → term → contact details → review), renewal, a DNS record manager, point-at-server, and
auto-renew.

**Dedicated IPv4.** `dedicated-ip.ts` **syncs** OVH failover IPs into a local pool (the worker
refreshes it every ~5 minutes). On a dedicated-IP order it **claims** a `FREE` IP, **creates the OVH
Virtual MAC** (an asynchronous OVH task, so the code polls until it appears), and attaches the VM to
`vmbr0` with that MAC and `ip=<IP>/32,gw=51.79.162.254`. Deleting the server **releases** the IP and
Virtual MAC back to the pool. The admin IP-pool page shows cost, revenue, and margin per IP. This
path is **verified end-to-end on real OVH IPs**.

**Multi-node.** Each `Node` row carries its own Proxmox credentials and IP/port pools. A scheduler
picks the **least-loaded enabled node** for a new server, and every worker handler is node-aware, so
the platform can span several physical hosts. `onboard-node.sh` prepares a fresh Proxmox host to join.
(Private networking *between* nodes would need a VPN/overlay — documented, not yet built.)

**Console (in-browser VM screen).** `/api/console/[serverId]` mints a **JWE** (an encrypted token,
single-use, 60-second lifetime) containing the Proxmox VNC target. The browser connects to
`wss://…/console-ws`, which nginx proxies to `console-proxy.mjs`; that relay validates the token and
pipes the stream to Proxmox's `vncwebsocket`. **The Proxmox ticket never reaches the browser.** The
noVNC client itself is vendored in `public/novnc`.

**RBAC (staff roles).** `rbac.ts` maps **areas to roles**: `SUPPORT` sees overview/clients/support;
`BILLING` sees billing/invoices/subscriptions/plans; `ADMIN` sees everything. `requireArea` guards
each admin page, and the admin layout admits any staff role while filtering the nav per role.
`/admin/staff` lets ADMINs assign roles.

**Email.** `mailer.ts` sends over SMTP (configured in admin Settings) with a local-Postfix fallback,
using branded templates — welcome, server-provisioned, payment receipt, renewal, suspension, and
password reset — wired into signup, payments, and the reset flow. `/admin/email-templates` shows a
**live iframe preview** of each template. (Real SMTP credentials are still required to actually send.)

**Monitoring & backups.** A **nightly database backup** and a **weekly VM backup** write to
`/tank/backup`, each with an `OnFailure` admin alert; journald is size-capped. The **improvement
agent** works the top roadmap item every 4 hours through the staging→promote pipeline.

All done. Everything is built, type-clean, and the production build passes.

## Summary

Built a complete, security-hardened in-portal web terminal for /opt/nxeon. Customers open it from the Claude Code hub, pick a running server, and get a real xterm.js root shell in a slide-in panel.

### Files created
- **`/opt/nxeon/lib/terminal-token.ts`** — shared JWE helper (mints/verifies encrypted 60s tokens). Imported by both the Next route and the standalone backend.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/api/terminal/token/route.ts`** — `POST {serverId}` token issuer.
- **`/opt/nxeon/terminal-server/index.ts`** — standalone `ws` + `ssh2` PTY backend (run by tsx, listens `127.0.0.1:8901`, outside `app/`, never imported by app code so Next won't bundle it).
- **`/opt/nxeon/deploy/nxeon-terminal.service`** — systemd unit.
- **`/opt/nxeon/deploy/nxeon-terminal.nginx.txt`** — nginx `location /terminal-ws` snippet.
- **`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/WebTerminal.tsx`** — `"use client"` slide-in panel (server `<select>`, Connect/Disconnect/Close, FitAddon + ResizeObserver, imports xterm CSS).

### Files modified
- **`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx`** — added the hero "Open terminal & start building" button (disabled with a deploy hint when no running server) and mounts `WebTerminal`.
- **`/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/claude-code/page.tsx`** — added `id` to the servers passed to the hub.
- **`/opt/nxeon/scripts/diag-email.ts`** — fixed a **pre-existing** build blocker unrelated to this work (queried `EmailLog.to`, the schema field is `toEmail`); it was failing `tsc`/`next build` before my changes. Corrected `to` → `toEmail`.
- **`/opt/nxeon/docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`** — added a "Web terminal" subsystem entry (per the standing docs instruction).
- **`package.json`** — added `@xterm/xterm@6`, `@xterm/addon-fit@0.11`, `ws@8`, devDep `@types/ws`. `ssh2@1.17` was already present.

### Token verification + ownership checks (exact)
- **Route** (`/api/terminal/token`): `requireUser()` (401 if unauthenticated) → rate-limit per user → `db.server.findUnique` selecting `{id,userId,status}` → reject unless `server.userId === user.id || user.role === "ADMIN"` (404) → reject unless `status === "RUNNING"` (409) → `signTerminalToken({userId, serverId})`. The token, not the session, authorizes the WS.
- **Token**: JWE, `alg:"dir", enc:"A256GCM"`, key = `sha256("nxeon-terminal:"+AUTH_SECRET)` (distinct salt from the console's `nxeon-console:` key so tickets aren't cross-replayable), `exp` = 60s enforced by `jwtDecrypt`. Payload carries only `{userId, serverId}`.
- **Backend** (`terminal-server`): reads `token` from the WS query string → `verifyTerminalToken` (throws/closes on missing/tampered/expired) → **re-loads the Server from the DB and re-checks `server.userId === claims.userId` and `status === "RUNNING"`** before any SSH → `connectionTarget(server)` for host/port → `serverRootPassword(server)` (decrypts `rootPasswordEnc`) → ssh2 PTY shell. Password never crosses the WS; SSH errors are surfaced to the client generically ("Could not connect…"), never logged.

### Timeouts enforced (backend)
- **15s** auth/connect deadline (token verify + SSH shell establishment; also passed as ssh2 `readyTimeout`).
- **10 min** idle (no bytes either direction) → close, with a notice.
- **60 min** hard session cap → close.
- Plus `keepaliveInterval` 20s, `{type:"resize",cols,rows}` → `stream.setWindow`, and clean bidirectional teardown on either side ending.

### Sandbox
When `SANDBOX` is set, after the same token + ownership checks, no SSH is opened — a friendly simulated echo shell is piped so staging works without real VMs.

### Verification results
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (excluding tests): **clean for all my files** (the only remaining project error was the pre-existing `diag-email.ts`, now fixed).
- `npm run build`: **exit 0**; `/api/terminal/token` registered as a route; `terminal-server/` correctly excluded from the Next bundle.
- Smoke test: `npx tsx terminal-server/index.ts` boots, loads env from `.env`, logs `listening on ws://127.0.0.1:PORT`, and binds `127.0.0.1` only.

One note for the parent/operator: the systemd unit and nginx snippet are written to `deploy/` for installation — the service must be installed/started and the nginx `location /terminal-ws` block (plus the `$connection_upgrade` map) added to the portal vhost for this to work in production. The existing CSP already allows `connect-src … wss:`.
